title: Imelda triggers catastrophic flash flooding in southeast Texas
primary_angle: Analyze the near-stationary inland tropical remnant, extreme moisture, and multiple short-duration rainfall maxima that prompted flash flood emergencies.
alternate_angle: Compare 12/24/48-hour precipitation windows and where localized catastrophic floods differed from Imelda's landfall site on September 17.
verified_core_fact: Remnants of Tropical Storm Imelda produced destructive flash flooding across southeast Texas on September 19, 2019.
graphic_type: Observed QPE maxima map and flash-flood warning timeline
research_note: Imelda made landfall on September 17, NOT September 19. WWA examines September 19–20 rainfall with independent attribution modeling but relies partly on NOAA rain data. Early fatality/property estimates not cleared; 1-in-1200 year station statistical probability is NOT a universal literal return interval. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-262703. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-406779, ncei-858116.

title: Tasmania records its wettest October day as major flooding develops
location: Northern Tasmania and Mersey–Meander basins, Australia
primary_angle: Explain how a slow-moving frontal rainband connected to tropical moisture dumped record 24-hour rain on saturated Tasmanian catchments.
alternate_angle: Compare the 24 hours ending 9 a.m. October 14 rainfall with subsequent river crest timing and evacuation warnings.
verified_core_fact: In the 24 hours to 9 a.m. October 14, 2022, Tasmania recorded its wettest October day statewide and widespread major flood warnings.
graphic_type: 24-hour station rainfall and catchment flood-response map
research_note: Meteorological daily rain is the 24h ending at 9 a.m. local, including rain on October 13. Do not attribute full multiday floods to the October 14 calendar day. BoM historical maps need asset-level reuse checks. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-923474. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-5716956, ncei-980123.

title: Tropical Storm Sandy forms in the southwest Caribbean
location: Southwestern Caribbean Sea south of Jamaica
source_publisher: NOAA National Hurricane Center historical advisory
primary_angle: Use the actual first advisories to show how a nascent October Caribbean tropical storm later developed a large wind field through multiple atmospheric interactions.
alternate_angle: Compare initial Oct 22 tropical formation south of Jamaica to post-tropical evolution much later without implying U.S. impacts happened that day.
verified_core_fact: Sandy reached tropical-storm intensity in the southwestern Caribbean on October 22, 2012.
graphic_type: Official best-track evolution with geoposition and day annotations
research_note: October 21 already has the 2007 Witch Creek Fire; choosing that event's Oct22 continuation would have repeated it. October 22 Sandy is formation, not storm surge nor U.S. landfall. Offshore center is explicitly labeled and not assigned to a landfall community. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-920645. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-5670346, ncei-200122.

title: Wildfire smoke blankets San Diego in a satellite-visible plume
location: San Diego County and southern California
primary_angle: Explain how October 27 smoke plumes and Santa Ana flow transformed a wildfire emergency into an exceptional regional air-quality crisis.
alternate_angle: Compare NASA's precisely dated Oct27 Aqua MODIS plume with verified October 27 PM2.5 filter measurements in San Diego County.
verified_core_fact: On October 27, 2003, a NASA Aqua satellite image showed immense wildfire smoke plumes from the Cedar, Paradise and Otay fires blanketing the San Diego region.
graphic_type: Original GOES/MODIS acquisition-time and air quality station comparison
research_note: Cedar and other fires ignited October 25–26, not October 27. Air Pollution Research paper reports Chula Vista PM2.5 24-hour filter maximum around 240 µg/m³ on Oct27; assess instrument records and whether a regional 24-h filter measurement can be compared with instantaneous satellite plume. No satellite media rights cleared. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-199043. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-855017, ncei-480568.

title: Post-tropical Noel enters Atlantic Canada's warning region
location: Atlantic Canada offshore waters and Maritime provinces
source_publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada / Canadian Hurricane Centre
primary_angle: Explain how Noel's transition from a tropical cyclone into an expansive extratropical gale altered the distribution of wind, rain and heavy seas.
alternate_angle: Use a 0000 UTC November 3 transformation timeline and Canadian warning zones without describing the November 4 Nova Scotia landfall as a November 3 event.
verified_core_fact: By the morning of November 3, 2007, Noel had become a large post-tropical storm and entered the Canadian Hurricane Centre response zone.
graphic_type: Extratropical transition and expanding wind-field timeline
research_note: NHC says extratropical transition was at 0000 UTC Nov 3. Subsequent Nova Scotia landfall was just AFTER 0600 UTC on Nov 4; do not call Nov3 a landfall day. Canadian archive is distinct from NHC but uses common storm-track data. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-1225079. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-346665, ncei-67789.

title: Former Hurricane Eta's flooding worsens across Honduras
source_publisher: NOAA National Hurricane Center / Weather Prediction Center
primary_angle: Show how Eta's movement across Central American mountains and persistent moisture feed generated dangerous flooding long after coastal landfall.
alternate_angle: Combine dated November 5 advisory center locations and later verified humanitarian flood footprints, avoiding final-loss estimates in early reports.
verified_core_fact: On November 5, 2020, Tropical Depression Eta remained over northern Honduras while the region endured significant flooding from the multiday cyclone.
graphic_type: Terrain, remnant center track and rainfall/landslide-hazard context
research_note: Eta made initial Nicaragua landfall on November 3 and caused multiday regional rainfall and landslides. November 5 is a Honduras flooding/remnant-circulation stage, not first landfall. UN assessment published November 7 summarizes prior impacts, not an independent November 5 meteorological observation. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-863855. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-1148655, ncei-727471.

title: Storm Bert sweeps Ireland with widespread heavy rain and storm-force winds
location: Ireland, including Mayo, Galway and Cork
primary_angle: Explain the sharp warm-frontal transition from pre-storm cold/snow into strong Atlantic winds and heavy rain.
alternate_angle: Contrast an authentic Nov23 Irish surface analysis with official 24-hour rain and station gust measurements, distinguishing daily totals and storm-wide accumulations.
verified_core_fact: Storm Bert brought widespread heavy rain and damaging winds to Ireland on Saturday, November 23, 2024.
graphic_type: Original station wind/rain map and surface-low evolution
research_note: The UK Met Office retrospective describes UK storm impacts and overlaps the same cyclone, but does not independently verify an individual Irish station report. Met Éireann's later review gives 57.4 mm at Knock Airport Nov23; a recorded station total is not all-Ireland precipitation. Storm Bert continued through Nov25. title: Arkansas River flooding breaks the previous stage record near Fort Smith
location: Fort Smith and Van Buren, Arkansas River valley
primary_angle: Trace how runoff moving downstream drove the Fort Smith gauge above its old stage record on May 28, before the river reached a higher later crest.
alternate_angle: Compare NASA's May 27/28 satellite-acquisition dates with the multi-day Arkansas River flood hydrograph and USGS finalized stage data.
verified_core_fact: NASA documents Arkansas River stage reaching 40.26 feet near Fort Smith on May 28, 2019, exceeding a prior 38.10-foot record; record flooding continued into June.
graphic_type: Original dated river-stage hydrograph and satellite comparison
research_note: May28 reached above previous flood record, but was NOT the final flood crest (later May30-31). NASA images dated May 27 and May 28 explicitly; do not mislabel those satellite dates or reuse without per-asset rights. NASA stage figure derives from hydrometric source, not a second independent gauge. Replaces 2019 Linwood EF4 tornado as primary to avoid May27-29 triple-tornado sequence; previous primary preserved: phasea-pass2-2019-05-28.
